steps.title: The Opening Question
steps.content:
So {{contact_first_name}}, how have things been since you finished the weight loss program with us? I usually hear one of three things. Still keeping the weight off, a little starting to creep back, or pretty much back to where you started. Which one is closest for you?

(Only three answers. Tap the one you hear.)

steps.title: Kept It Off
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes a program with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still doing well.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: A Little Crept Back
steps.content:
Thanks for telling me, {{contact_first_name}}. A little creeping back almost never means the program didn't work. It usually means life pulled you away from the routine. The plan is built to be picked back up.

(Let them answer. No blame in your voice.)

A lot of people try other things in between, like the shots or an app. Did you try anything like that?

(Ask it lightly. If they mention GLP shots or injections, tap that button below.)

I'm glad I caught you. This is the kind of thing we want to know about.

(Do not pitch anything yet. The file questions come next.)

steps.title: Mostly or All Back
steps.content:
Thank you for being honest with me, {{contact_first_name}}. You did not fail. The program worked, and you lost the weight. What didn't happen was the follow-up, and that's the part we get right this time.

(Let them answer. No blame. It's "life happened," never "you didn't follow it.")

A lot of people try other things in between, like the shots or an app. Did you try anything like that?

(Ask it lightly. If they mention GLP shots or injections, tap that button below.)

I'm glad I caught you. This is the kind of thing we want to know about.

(Do not pitch anything yet. The file questions come next.)

steps.title: They Tried GLP Shots In Between
steps.content:
(They have watched two approaches "fail" them. Take the shame off first. No smugness.)

I understand why you tried it, {{contact_first_name}}. Those medications do work while you're on them, and everyone was talking about them. You don't owe anyone an apology.

(Pause.)

Can I share what I think you learned from all of it? The medication did the work for you, so the results left when it did. Our program worked too, and it came with a plan for keeping the weight off. That's the part that didn't get its turn last time.

So your body isn't broken, and it's not true that nothing works. You've proven the weight loss program takes the weight off. Round two is where we focus on keeping it off.

(Do not pitch or schedule here. Continue to the file questions.)

steps.title: Booked: Wrap Up
steps.content:
Perfect, you're all set for (day) at (time), {{contact_first_name}}.

Come in just as you are. No dieting before the visit, and no worrying about the scale. We'll take a look together and get you back on the plan that keeps it off.

We look forward to seeing you.

steps.title: The Review
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, let me make sure I have this right.

(Recap what they told you: how long, how often, how it affects them.)

Did I get that right?

And it sounds like you'd like to get back to how you felt when things were going well. Is that fair to say?

(Most people say yes. Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate: Find Out Why
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, you said {{main_concern}} is something you'd like to feel better about. I don't want to assume anything. Is it the timing, or is something else holding you back?

(Stay easy about it. No pressure. Do not repeat the concern back at them. Let them answer.)

steps.title: The Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, while I have you, I'd like to get your file up to date. Can I ask you a few quick questions?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Ask these in order. Write down everything they mention. You'll read it back in a moment.)

You said some of the weight has come back. About how much are we talking?

Are the eating habits you built during the program still mostly in place?

How's your energy through the day, any afternoon crashes?

How have you been sleeping?

Do you feel irritable or under a lot of stress?

Any allergy or sinus problems, even ones you think are normal?

Any pain, stiffness, or soreness in your neck or back, even if it's mild?

What about your knees, hips, or feet?

Any headaches, even mild ones that go away on their own?

And are you taking any medications, prescribed or over the counter?

(Read back what they mentioned, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below. If they named nothing new, use the weight-focus button.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about {{main_concern}} so your file is up to date. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Write down the answers. Pause after each.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a month or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you notice like a few days a month, or is it most days?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask a few quick questions about {{main_concern}} so your file is up to date. It'll only take a minute.

(Ask these three questions in order. Write down the answers. Pause after each.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It makes sense, and it's something we help people with all the time.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, it sounds like {{main_concern}} isn't just affecting you. It may be getting in the way at home or at work too. Do you see how that could be the case?

(Wait for the answer. If they hesitate, say "That's fair. It's still been bothering you, and that's reason enough." Then continue.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If we can help, we'll tell you. If it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: The Recommendation: Weight Focus
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, can I say something? You've already done the hardest part. You proved you can lose the weight, because you did it. What's happening now is drift, and drift is easier to fix than starting over. Does that make sense?

(Wait for the yes.)

{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

My recommendation is that we get you in so {{provider_name}} can see where things are. Then we help you get back to where you were. If we can help, we'll tell you. If it's not the right fit, we'll tell you that too. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Kept It Off: The Check-In Close
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's part of why I'm calling. The plan works best with a check-in now and then. We look at where you are and make sure the guidelines still fit your life. Think of it as protecting the win.

Let's get you on the schedule. We have time this week on (day) at (time) or (day) at (time). Which is better for you?

steps.title: Objection: “I should do it myself this time”
steps.content:
I understand, and that's a good mindset. Coming back in just gives you the support and structure that made it work the first time. We can map that out with you.

Would that help?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’m embarrassed I gained it back”
steps.content:
Please don't be. There's no judgment here. Life gets in the way of even the best routines. The important thing is you already know the program works for you. We'd just like to help you get back to where you were.

Would you be open to that?

steps.title: Objection: Cost (weight is the focus)
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. This first visit is just a look. You're not committing to anything. Can I ask how much getting back there matters to you? The way you felt in your clothes, the energy, all of it.

(Let them answer. This is the question that does the work.)

One more thing. Depending on where things stand, you may not need the full program again. If only some of the weight came back, a shorter course is often enough. That's what the visit figures out.

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

Can we at least get you in so we can see where you're at?

steps.title: The Transition: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, while I have you, I'd like to get your file up to date. Can I ask you a few quick questions?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: The Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Ask these in order. Write down everything they mention. You'll read it back in a moment.)

Is the weight still holding steady, or has any started to creep back?

Are the eating habits you built during the program still mostly in place?

How's your energy through the day, any afternoon crashes?

How have you been sleeping?

Do you feel irritable or under a lot of stress?

Any allergy or sinus problems, even ones you think are normal?

Any pain, stiffness, or soreness in your neck or back, even if it's mild?

What about your knees, hips, or feet?

Any headaches, even mild ones that go away on their own?

And are you taking any medications, prescribed or over the counter?

(Read back what they mentioned, then ask:)

{{contact_first_name}}, of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below. If nothing new came up, use the check-in close.)

steps.title: Objection: “I thought that was behind me”
steps.content:
That's a fair thing to bring up. These things can creep back over time with everyday wear and tear. It doesn't mean anything went wrong. That's the kind of thing we'd want to look at in person.

Can we get you in for a look?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Objection: “I’ve seen a chiropractor. It didn’t help”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm glad you told me. No two offices approach this the same way. A lot of it comes down to finding what's really causing the problem. That's what the visit is for.

If we can help with {{main_concern}}, we'll tell you. If we can't, we'll tell you that too.

Is there anything else on your mind?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think about it”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Can I ask what part you'd want to think over? Sometimes it's the cost, sometimes the timing, and sometimes people want to be sure it's the right fit.

(Listen. Their answer usually points to one of the buttons below. If it stays general, keep going.)

Coming in is really just information. We look at where you're at with {{main_concern}}, and you decide with real answers. If it's not the right fit, we'll tell you.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Just send me some info”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send you some information, {{contact_first_name}}. The one thing I'd say is that a flyer can only tell you so much. It can't look at where you're at right now. That's what the visit is for. So let me get you on the schedule first, and then I'll send the information along.

Does that work for you?
